text:
mia: FYI ran the long-horizon kvcache synthetic this morning and hit steady memory growth across runs (~2GB over 8M tokens). reproducer attached below.

jordan: ugh, same harness as last week? which branch/commit?

mia: master at time of run (commit 9f3a2b1). bench command: `./bench --suite long-horizon --kv-cap=8g --seq-dist=wide --steps=100000 --seed=42`

vasil: can you paste the perf summary? especially kvcache eviction/alloc metrics.

mia: perf excerpt: 
```
KVCache: alloc_bytes=8.12G resident=7.9G evictions=3124 compactions=2 frag_pct=14.3
Alloc churn: allocs/s=120 evict_calls/s=3.1 reuse_hits=0.62
LongCtx: avg_kv_entries=512k kv_lookup_latency_p95=1.9ms
```

leo: reuse_hits 0.62 is low for this workload — suggests poor fragment reuse leading to extra allocations. did you enable slab rotation?

mia: yes slab_rot=true in config. also saw periodic bursts of `kv_alloc()` time in pprof stack sample around `choose_kernel_for_write` and `alloc_extent` stacking.

perf-bot: sample flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/test/2176543210/flame.svg (shows heavy time in kernel selector when sequence_len > 1024).

jordan: interesting — kernel selection path might be doing expensive checks per extent. that could serialize things and prevent reuse. can you capture a trace with KV_DEBUG=1?

mia: attached small trace (first 30s) and heap profile `/tmp/heap-2176543210.pb.gz`. grep'ed for alloc hot paths: 
```
# top 5 symbols
choose_kernel_for_write 38%
alloc_extent 21%
kv_insert_probe 12%
kv_compact_run 10%
continuous_batcher::flush 5%
```

vasil: kv_compact_run at 10% but compactions only 2 — suggests compaction is heavy when it runs, likely full-copy style which fragments more. can you enable incremental_compact=true and rerun?

mia: will try incremental_compact, but note this reproduces even on small batch sizes (batch=1) so batching heuristics aren't the primary driver. however, I did notice `continuous_batcher::flush` spikes correlate with eviction waves.

leo: eviction waves + heavy kernel selection + compaction = perfect storm for transient memory spikes that then don't recycle due to fragmentation. test suggestion: run long-horizon with `--kv-prealloc=1` to force fixed extents and `--enable-incr-compact` and compare max_resident.

mia: quick patch run results (30m): prealloc + incr compact dropped growth from 2.0GB -> 0.18GB over same token count. numbers: 
```
baseline_max_rss=9.8G patched_max_rss=8.02G delta=1.78G
evictions baseline=3124 patched=2800 reuse_hits patched=0.88
```

jordan: good signal. can you add a focused regression test to our CI long-context suite that toggles prealloc + incr compact and asserts max_rss delta < 300MB after 100k steps? aim for a tiny, deterministic harness.

mia: plan: add `tests/longhorizon/kv_frag_repro.rs` with two runs (baseline, patched) using `--seed=1` and compare peak_rss. will add measurements to the perf dashboard and include pprof artifacts.

ops-bot: heads up — if we add prealloc to default, ephemeral Dedicated instances may need bigger disk pressure checks. also file a sizing note for infra.

vasil: also add a telemetry counter for `kv_reuse_ratio` and `kv_frag_pct` so we can monitor in prod. cheap metric.

mia: noted. I'll open a PR with the test + metric + docs for the config flags. tagging @jordan @vasil for review. :memo:

jordan: thanks — if CI reproduces flaky failures, we should backport compaction fix to the 1.x branch.

mia: will follow up with PR link when ready. thanks everyone. :+1:
